overall: Atlanta is experiencing a warm, humid early afternoon with the running max reaching 82.9°F by 13:30 ET. Warming has stalled momentarily (velocity near 0°F/hr at the observation time), with 62% cloud cover and scattered skies limiting insolation. Active severe weather alerts (Flash Flood Warnings, Flood Advisories) are confined to southeast Georgia and northeast Florida — well south of Atlanta — and do not directly threaten today's temperature peak, though a slight chance of afternoon thunderstorms after 2pm could suppress further warming.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in strong agreement, clustering tightly between 83.9°F (HRRR) and 84.9°F (ECMWF/NBM), all pointing to a peak roughly 1-2°F above the current running max. The NWS text forecast of near 86°F sits at the upper end of model guidance. The timing models (NWP mean 16:00h, intraday model 14.6h) suggest the peak is still 1-3 hours ahead, but the flat velocity at 13:30 and substantial cloud fraction introduce uncertainty about how much additional warming can materialize.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 82.9°F, NWP models targeting 83.9–84.9°F, and the slight post-2pm thunderstorm threat potentially capping afternoon heating, the most likely outcome is a daily high in the 84–86°F range. The META model concentrates 58% of probability in 84–87°F and the INTRADAY model puts 59% in 84–87°F as well, consistent with models. A final high near 84.5–85°F is the central estimate, with upside to 86°F possible if clouds scatter and no convective activity develops over Atlanta proper. Confidence is moderate given the stalled warming trend and cloud cover.
